planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: Phase 24: «كل الميزانيات محقّقة ومفروضة في CI» — budgets enforced in CI.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: No browser-measured budget CAN block a merge today: all 17 live guards run with blocking:false and continue-on-error, by a deliberate documented decision. So a phase-24 budget added as a new verify:* guard would be 'in CI' and simultaneously unable to fail the build. The workflow states the promotion rule (ten consecutive green rounds → blocking:true), which means 'enforced' requires either that promotion or attaching the budget to the blocking job (where only the static bundle budget, 24أ, can live).
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml — 17 matrix entries all `{ guard: X, blocking: false }`; `continue-on-error: ${{ !matrix.blocking }}`; comment at :114 'قاعدة الترقية … عشر جولات خضراء متتالية'; measured 4-round stability record in the same comment (capture, compare-diff, load, popup at 0/4). The blocking job runs typecheck/tokens/lint/format/test/build/verify:dist only.

openQuestions: MEASURED BUNDLE NUMBERS, for the record (clean build, today): dist total 1.1M via du -sh; verify:dist reports 1020.6 KB across 57 files. dist/content.js = 323,707 B raw, 90,304 B gzip -9 = 88.2 KB vs the ≤120KB budget (74% used, ~32KB headroom). Popup graph = entry index.html-MKWD0apl.js 6,110 gz + Icon 17,501 + IconButton 1,233 + ProgressBar 322 + TechnicalValue 325 + permissions 1,911 + repository 3,771 + rpc 934 = 32,107 B gz JS, plus 6 stylesheets (fonts 937, tokens 5,192, base 1,888, IconButton 1,319, ProgressBar 258, index 2,228) = 11,822 B gz → ≈43 KB gz total vs the ≤80KB budget. BOTH PHASE-24 SIZE BUDGETS ALREADY PASS.

What does «مضغوطة» mean in the budget table — gzip or brotli? I measured gzip -9. It matters: content.js is 316 KB raw but 88 KB gzipped, and the Chrome Web Store ships the bundle uncompressed, so the raw figure is what a reviewer sees while the gz figure is what a user downloads. 24أ should pin this in one line before writing the gate.

Which Lighthouse route? Three live options, and the plan's chosen one rests on a premise that no longer holds: (a) playwright-lighthouse — requires Playwright, which does not exist in any form and is phase 23's deliverable; (b) the lighthouse MCP now present in this environment — needs a probe that it can audit a locally launched Chrome carrying an unpacked extension, before/after injection; (c) chrome-launcher + the existing raw-CDP harness, which already spawns Chrome with --remote-debugging-port and would avoid a second automation stack entirely. This decision gates 24د, 25ج's ≥95 item, and three previously deferred Lighthouse steps (phases 5, 10, 19). It deserves an ADR, not an inline choice.

Does phase 25 really depend on phase 24? The plan declares «الاعتماديات: المراحل 22 و23 و24» for 25, but the ONLY coupling I can find in either text is inherited item #5 — the idle-overlay CPU measurement, which 25 merely documents while 24 measures. Nothing in the a11y, security, permissions or privacy work consumes a performance number. If that reading holds, 24 and 25 are genuinely parallel (and 25أ is parallel to everything, needing no browser at all).

The offscreen decision may already be forced by ordering. Phase 19 (export — WebP/PDF, the plan's named 'natural consumer') runs BEFORE 25 in the ADR-0013 order. If 19 ships export without routing encoding through the offscreen document, branch (أ) has no remaining rationale and 25أ's 'binary decision' collapses to deletion. Worth telling phase 19 explicitly, since it is the one that decides.

src/modules/a11y/role.ts has ZERO production importers (grep -rn 'modules/a11y' src/ → empty) — only its own unit test uses it. Phase 25 item #4 asks for an ADR codifying what this module approximates. Should we codify a module nothing calls, delete it, or wire it into the inspect panel (src/ui/overlay/inspect/InspectPanel.tsx, which today shows no role/name row)? Wiring it is phase-11 scope creep; deleting it contradicts an explicit phase-25 deliverable. Needs a call.

The contrast gate in 25ب will go red on a defect it is not allowed to fix. Rasd_Plan.md:1985 (contradiction #10) records --rasd-text-tertiary (#687c87) at 4.04–4.35 on light backgrounds, under AA 4.5, live in Input placeholder and Menu section titles — assigned to phase 26 because the fix must come from the Figma source (ADR 0007 forbids hand-editing the generated tokens.css). Either sequence 25ب after 26أ, or have the gate carry one named, dated exemption.

Can a phase-24/25 budget be 'enforced in CI' at all right now? All 17 live guards are non-blocking by a documented decision, and the measured 4-round record in ci.yml shows the set of failing guards moving every round (capture, compare-diff, load and popup at 0/4) — a common environment cause the workflow itself assigns to phase 23. Any new perf or a11y guard joins that same non-blocking pool unless it can live in the blocking job, which only the static bundle budget (24أ) can.

A pre-existing security note, not a phase-25 finding but adjacent: web_accessible_resources declares matches: ['<all_urls>'] with three glob patterns (assets/fonts/*, assets/overlay/*, assets/*.css). use_dynamic_url: true is set, which defeats fingerprinting, and manifest.config.ts:106-109 explains the globs are needed because CRXJS requires named files to exist at build time. Phase 25 asks for «أضيق مطابقة ممكنة» — narrowing matches below <all_urls> may be impossible for an extension whose whole purpose is injecting into arbitrary pages, so this item may resolve as 'documented, not narrowed'.
